papers.title: Atria Dawn: The Dawn of Agentic Superintelligence

summary.tldr: Atria Dawn Preview is a foundation agentic language model for scientific research and engineering trained via a Verifiable Experience Pipeline.
key_points: Trained using a Verifiable Experience Pipeline connecting tool-mediated interactions to executable environments and verified outcomes.
Evaluated across 16 benchmarks covering research, engineering, and digital work, achieving the highest reported score on five of them.
Analyzed human-AI collaboration across 769 task records from 56 participants alongside agent logs.
Participants rated roughly one-third of completed AI-assisted tasks as infeasible without AI assistance.
Identified a collaboration shift where agents propose methods and execute revisions while humans handle final decisions, feedback, and high-level project direction.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how agentic models can handle complex, execution-heavy research tasks while keeping human researchers focused on high-level oversight and project direction.

papers.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds

summary.tldr: Dream-RSI is a recursive self-improvement framework that uses historical discovery trees as replay simulators to optimize AI agent exploration policies via low-cost off-policy feedback.
key_points: Uses a lightweight orchestration layer that makes exploration programmable without altering the underlying coding agent.
Constructs a replay simulator from accumulated discovery history to provide immediate, low-cost off-policy feedback.
Avoids expensive online policy evaluations during dreaming before redeploying refined policies to expand the search space.
Validated across algorithm engineering, mathematical optimization, and GPU kernel engineering.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables autonomous AI agents to continuously improve their exploration strategies in complex domains while significantly reducing computational search costs.

papers.title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search

summary.tldr: ZGCM-1 is an open-source 7B foundation model designed for mathematical reasoning and agentic search across a 256K context window.
key_points: Architecture uses interleaved gated sliding-window and full attention trained via a stable FP8 Muon optimizer, yielding a ~4.2x efficiency improvement in 16K pre-training time-to-loss.
Employs a progressive context scaling curriculum (16K to 64K to 256K) and reformulates tool interaction traces into Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) during mid-training.
Utilized an AI-native workflow where autonomous agent swarms managed cluster operations, data curation, and diagnostic evaluations.
Open-sources full lifecycle assets including model weights across all stages, intermediate checkpoints, training code, data recipes, and W&B logs.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that compact 7B models can match much larger frontier models like Qwen3-235B-A22B on math and agentic search by combining long-context deliberate reasoning with active tool use.

papers.title: PhysBrain 1.5: From Vision-Language Models to Physical Foundation Models

summary.tldr: PhysBrain 1.5 is an 8B physical foundation model that unifies embodied understanding, action generation, and future state prediction using unified autoregressive next-token prediction.
key_points: Encodes language responses, end-effector motion, and dense visual targets as discrete sequences within a vision-language model architecture.
Pre-trains entirely on human interaction videos to pair semantic and spatial context with recovered motion and subsequent observations.
Fine-tunes on a mixture of human demonstrations, robot trajectories, and simulated experience.
Achieves a 72.5 average score across 28 benchmarks, matching proprietary models like GPT-6-Astra and Gemini 3.6 Flash, while topping open-source results on 14 benchmarks.
Predicts future scenes via spatially aligned RGB, depth, and robot-mask outputs while generating end-effector trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a single open-source 8B model can achieve state-of-the-art embodied physical reasoning and future-state prediction while maintaining general vision-language capabilities.

papers.title: LynnReal-Omni: Native multi-modal Video Generation for Agentic Visual Workflows

summary.tldr: LynnReal-Omni introduces a native multimodal video generation framework using 32B base and 27B Flash shared multimodal diffusion transformers to unify text, reference image, structural control, and editing conditions.
key_points: Built on a shared multimodal diffusion transformer architecture (32B base model and 27B Flash model) to unify T2V, image conditioning, structural control, editing, and video restoration.
Supports input from agentic visual sources, including appearance references, editable 3D renders, and game recordings.
Accelerates real-time rendering via model optimization and a lightweight VAE decoder, reducing 22-frame 540p video generation and decoding times on an H100 GPU from 843 ms (Omni) to 377 ms (Flash).
Establishes a curated multi-shot audiovisual training pipeline and introduces MSAVP, an evaluation framework using 100 prompts across 20 metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, highly controllable, and coherent streaming video generation required for interactive, agent-driven visual workflows.

papers.title: ReactHuman: A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Human-Like Reactive Decision-Making in Embodied Multimodal LLMs

summary.tldr: ReactHuman is a new physics-grounded benchmark containing over 1,000 reproducible 240 Hz simulated scenes across 17 event families designed to evaluate multimodal LLMs on immediate, safety-critical reactive decision-making during sudden physical hazards.
key_points: Features 17 event families and over 1,000 bit-for-bit reproducible scenes using 240 Hz rigid-body simulation, including adversarial objects like foam anvils.
Evaluates MLLM decisions by physically executing committed plans to produce observable consequences assessed across five metrics covering reasonable, safe, and physically grounded axes.
Evaluated seven representative MLLMs and found models mishandle ~33% of hazards, rely on fixed dispositions, trust appearance over motion, and miss interception points by meters.
Identified that reactive safety failures do not decrease with larger model scale.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes critical safety and physical reasoning gaps in current MLLMs, showing that scaling model size alone is insufficient to prepare embodied agents for real-world physical hazards.

papers.title: Discovery Foundation Models: Toward Open-Ended Discovery Intelligence

summary.tldr: Discovery Foundation Models (DFMs) expand foundation models beyond human-specified tasks into open-ended knowledge creation using a seven-capability framework operating over a revisable research state.
key_points: Formulates DFMs around seven coupled capabilities: problem discovery, formulation, representation construction, hypothesis formation, intervention, evidence-grounded revision, and continual discovery improvement.
Instantiates the framework via Zetema, incorporating explicit research-state dynamics, verification/experimental gating, external grounding, and cross-task Discovery Skill evolution.
Demonstrates practical implementation with GALILEO, a therapeutic-discovery system combining Dry-Lab reasoning and Wet-Lab robotic/hands-on experimentation in a closed physical loop.
Introduces process-centered evaluation to train, measure, and improve discovery behaviors rather than relying solely on final-answer performance metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: DFMs transition AI systems from executing predefined human tasks to autonomously generating, testing, and revising original scientific knowledge across physical and digital domains.

papers.title: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments

summary.tldr: RSIAgent is a training-free, multi-agent framework that uses autonomous memory construction and a broad-then-deep exploration strategy to enable recursive self-improvement in new environments.
key_points: Coordinates curriculum, actor, and verifier agents to explore environments, validate outcomes, and retain reusable causal relationships without updating weights.
Employs a broad-then-deep strategy: parallel broad exploration discovers environment structures while deep exploration targets edge cases, hidden constraints, and unknown causal dependencies.
Produces a frozen memory representation that can be directly applied to downstream tasks.
Enables open-source models Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3 to surpass closed-source models such as GPT-6 on OSWorld-v2 and Agent's Last Exam benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows digital agents to rapidly adapt to unfamiliar interfaces and tools without requiring computationally expensive parameter updates or fine-tuning.

papers.title: BVB: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding via Programmatic Reconstruction in Blender

summary.tldr: Blender-VideoBench (BVB) evaluates agentic video understanding by requiring multimodal agents to programmatically reconstruct real-world videos as animated 3D Blender scenes within a shared sandbox harness.
key_points: Agents execute code via Mini-BVB, a lightweight harness with shared cost constraints and animated camera rendering.
Evaluation uses two metrics: Dual VQA for spatiotemporal fact preservation and Latent Similarity for perceptual alignment, combined via a square-root mean.
Benchmarking 51 configurations across 10 model families showed a top Latent Similarity of 88.6, but a maximum spatiotemporal answer retention of only 53.7%.
A blind human study with 15 raters across 5 configurations confirmed a strong correlation between Latent Similarity and human preference.
Increasing reasoning effort improved visual similarity metrics but failed to close the semantic retention gap.
summary.why_it_matters: BVB shifts video understanding evaluation from basic question answering to generative programmatic reconstruction, highlighting semantic retention as the primary bottleneck for multimodal agents.

papers.title: AlayaVista: Streaming World Modeling from Panoramic States to Perspective Video

summary.tldr: AlayaVista is a camera-controllable streaming video world model that decouples 360-degree panoramic latent state evolution from perspective video synthesis to maintain broad scene context with low latency.
key_points: Constructs a 360-degree scene prior from a single perspective image using a pretrained panorama expansion model.
Evolves the scene as a camera-conditioned panoramic latent state, mapping it to perspective video latents via a latent viewport renderer.
Applies a perspective refiner to restore details, suppress artifacts, and perform super-resolution on output frames.
Adapts the panoramic generator to chunk-autoregressive generation and distills generation and refinement modules into few-step processes for streaming efficiency.
Introduces MUGEN, a real-world panoramic video dataset comprising 1,318 hours of 4K+ resolution video with semantic and geometric annotations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables low-latency, interactive video generation that maintains long-term, off-screen spatial consistency without the computational overhead of full 3D scene reconstruction.

papers.title: Pelican-Sim 1.0: A General World Model Simulator for Embodied Intelligence

summary.tldr: Pelican-Sim 1.0 is a general world model simulator that leverages unified action representations, MoE layers, action-video injection, and distillation to achieve controllable, high-speed rollout generation for embodied AI.
key_points: Employs a 28-dimensional unified action space to support heterogeneous robot embodiments within a single model.
Bridges actions and visual context using URDF- and camera-rendered action videos, achieving a +0.904 PSNR gain over alternative fusion baselines.
Uses sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers to absorb action modalities and reduce inter-modality conflict, improving FVD by -6.530 compared to a dense backbone.
Applies causal adaptation and few-step distillation to reduce autoregressive generation from 35 steps to 4 steps, yielding a 5.67-fold speedup.
Augmenting 50 real demonstrations per task with 500 Pelican-Sim generated trajectories increases downstream policy success rates from 70% to 93% on RoboTwin.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that fast, controllable video-based world models can significantly boost real-world robot policy performance, evaluation accuracy, and data scaling across diverse embodiments.

papers.title: How Lossless Is Lossless Speculative Decoding? The Role of Numerical Precision in Orthrus

summary.tldr: An independent reproduction of the hybrid autoregressive-diffusion model Orthrus reveals that its speculative decoding exact-trajectory match drops to 43-45% under BF16 precision, achieving 100% exact matching only under FP32 precision.
key_points: Orthrus achieves 100% exact trajectory matching under FP32 precision across evaluated prompts, confirming numerical precision dictates its exact losslessness.
Under BF16 precision, exact trajectory matching falls to 45% on the authors' checkpoint and 43% on an independently trained model across 1,190 prompts from 12 domains.
The probability of an exact trajectory match under BF16 correlates strongly with the response-conditional perplexity of the reference model.
Trajectory divergence under lower precision does not cause systematic degradation on downstream lm-eval-harness benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating losslessness in speculative decoding architectures requires separating strict output trajectory equivalence, which depends heavily on numerical precision, from downstream benchmark performance.

papers.title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level

summary.tldr: KaiNinja extends native 3D generators like TRELLIS.2 to part-level generation using a dual-volume representation, eliminating post-hoc 3D segmentation.
key_points: Introduces a dual-volume O-Voxel representation to resolve surface-sheet collisions at part interfaces within a single volume grid.
Eliminates masks and segmentation networks from the inference pipeline, preserving the speed and fidelity of the TRELLIS.2 backbone.
Incorporates training data from diverse sources, including CAD models and LLM-driven agent-authored part assets.
Outperforms existing part generation pipelines by reducing whole-object Chamfer distance by 40% and increasing strict part F-score by 16%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables direct single-image generation of segmented, editable 3D part assets required for downstream rigging, editing, and simulation without speed or quality trade-offs.

papers.title: Omni-Streaming Thinking

summary.tldr: Omni-Streaming Thinking (OST) resolves premature cross-modal commitment in streaming omni-modal models by decoupling visual/audio evidence, marking claims as pending for later verification, and executing refutations upon detecting contradictory evidence.
key_points: Separates audio and visual evidence storage, linking pending claims to future verification intervals for modality-specific validation.
Uses a refutation process upon detecting contradictions to reduce the influence of invalid claims and update states before an answer gate permits output.
Built on a frozen Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct backbone with lightweight adaptation.
Outperforms open baselines by >10% relative on average across five streaming/audio-visual benchmarks.
Achieves d-prime = 2.95 on the new OST-DiagBench compared to <=1.38 for open baselines, mitigating vision-induced auditory hallucinations.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents real-time multimodal models from locking into incorrect early assumptions when visual inputs prematurely contradict evolving audio streams.

papers.title: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents

summary.tldr: LLaDA-UI introduces a 16.7B-parameter MoE block-wise diffusion vision-language model designed for latency-sensitive multimodal GUI agent tasks.
key_points: LLaDA-UI utilizes a 16.7B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) block-wise diffusion vision-language architecture.
The model undergoes a two-stage training pipeline: native-resolution vision encoder alignment with the LLaDA2.0-mini-base backbone, followed by cross-platform GUI supervised fine-tuning.
It outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-7B across evaluated benchmarks and surpasses Qwen3-VL-8B on four out of six reported GUI benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that block-wise diffusion LLMs can serve as high-performing, fast-decoding vision-language backbones for real-time GUI navigation and grounding.

papers.title: HazardAuditor: From Executable Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents

summary.tldr: HazardAuditor is an execution-grounded framework that normalizes runtime agent behaviors into canonical events and uses Guard Policy Optimization (GuardPO) to train generative safety guards on computer-use tasks.
key_points: Runs heterogeneous computer-use agents (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw) in controlled runtime environments like browsers, terminals, and file systems.
Normalizes diverse agent interactions into a canonical event representation for cross-framework supervision.

Introduces Guard Policy Optimization (GuardPO) to solve token-level post-training mismatches by converting deterministic outcomes into sequence-level advantages and normalizing rationale and verdict regions.
Outperforms prior safety guards by up to 16.5 percentage points in accuracy across multiple benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables effective, cross-framework safety guarding for computer-use agents by evaluating real-time execution risks rather than relying on static text prompts.

papers.title: When Agents Slow Down: Understanding LLM Agents' Test-Time Strategies via Elo-per-token Analysis

summary.tldr: Elo-per-token analysis uses a Bradley-Terry model on continuous scores to evaluate LLM agent scaling efficiency, revealing that agents eventually suffer diminishing marginal returns compared to independent sampling.
key_points: Tracks agent progress using Elo-per-token analysis, applying a Bradley-Terry model to convert continuous intermediate scores into comparative Elo ratings across tasks.
Establishes that independent sampling yields a linear growth of Elo relative to log compute, serving as a baseline reference.

Shows agents initially outperform independent sampling in token efficiency, but their marginal gains diminish and eventually fall below the baseline, unlike top human contestants who exhibit superlinear improvement.

Defines a scaling inflection point where agent marginal Elo matches independent sampling, and demonstrates that splitting a 100M token budget into parallel sessions based on this point gains +264 Elo over a single long session.
summary.why_it_matters: Identifying an agent's scaling inflection point allows developers to optimize compute allocation by splitting monolithic agent runs into parallel sessions before diminishing returns set in.

papers.title: Not All Prompts Are Equal: Exploration-Guided Prompt Scaffolding for Multimodal Reinforcement Post-Training

summary.tldr: A new framework uses an Exploration Potential Score to dynamically adjust training prompt distributions and apply teacher-generated prompt rewrites during multimodal reinforcement post-training.
key_points: Introduces the Exploration Potential Score (EPS), a rollout-based proxy derived from KL-regularized policy improvement theory to measure prompt utility without extra overhead.
Reframes teacher model supervision by using teacher-generated scaffolded prompt rewrites to refine uninformative prompts while preserving task intent.
Integrates with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and evaluated on Geo3K and MMK12 benchmarks.
Achieves up to 9.7% relative in-domain improvement and out-of-distribution gains of 11.5% on MathVision and 11.1% on MMMU-Pro.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves RL efficiency and model generalization by allocating rollout budgets to prompts with high learning value rather than wasting compute on saturated or overly difficult tasks.

papers.title: Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation

summary.tldr: Agent as Policy (AGP) enables general-purpose agents to directly drive physical robots using runtime visual reasoning, program synthesis, and continuous motion command revisions without task-specific or environment-specific training.
key_points: AGP integrates task planning and execution by having the agent interpret visual input, generate executable code, and issue real-time motion commands.
The system autonomously revises its physical actions based on real-world execution outcomes and feedback.
Tested across diverse real-world tasks including human video assembly, die reorientation, throwing, bimanual towel folding, and block construction.
Achieved success rates of 100%, 100%, and 80% across three distinct block construction test configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that general-purpose AI agents can handle complex physical manipulation directly through runtime reasoning and code generation without requiring specialized training data.

papers.title: Pick Your Poison: Learning to Select Poison Sets for Stronger LLM Backdoor Attacks

summary.tldr: SAILS formalizes poison set selection as set optimization, using a learned set scorer trained on hundreds of audit runs to select highly effective poison subsets that outperform traditional influence baselines.
key_points: Random sampling of poison sets underestimates worst-case vulnerability, with attack success ranging from 3% to 80% on LLaMA-3-8B under identical clean data and poison count conditions.
SAILS (Set-level Audit-Informed Iterative Learned Selection) trains a set scorer on a few hundred finetune-and-evaluate runs, ranks millions of candidate sets, and audits a small shortlist.
SAILS improves held-out attack success rate by an average of 30 percentage points over strong influence-based baselines.
The method demonstrates transferability from small-scale to full-scale finetuning and works across code-generation, agentic, and API-only backdoor scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating backdoor risks using random poison sampling significantly underestimates model vulnerability, necessitating set-optimization frameworks like SAILS for realistic security auditing.

papers.title: Attention-DP3: Spatially Object-aware 3D Diffusion Policy via Geometry-aligned Attentional Conditioning

summary.tldr: Attention-DP3 enhances 3D diffusion policies by lifting open-vocabulary 2D RGB segmentation masks into 3D and conditioning the diffusion backbone using a Tri-field Attentional Conditioning mechanism.
key_points: Lifts 2D open-vocabulary segmentation masks to 3D via calibrated camera geometry to generate object-centric geometric priors.
Introduces Tri-field Attentional Conditioning featuring a targetness field, an intra-target saliency field, and a backgroundness field to emphasize targets and suppress clutter.
Preserves the underlying DP3 diffusion backbone architecture without direct modifications.
Outperforms standard DP3 by up to 31% in success rates under heavy clutter across Adroit, DexArt, MetaWorld, and real-world SO101 hardware.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents policy performance degradation in complex, cluttered manipulation environments by robustly isolating task-relevant geometry from distractor objects.

papers.title: Studying Without a Syllabus: Task-Agnostic Environment Preprocessing

summary.tldr: A new framework formalizes task-agnostic environment preprocessing, enabling LLM agents to explore environments and build reusable artifacts without downstream task distributions or syllabus supervision.
key_points: Formalizes task-agnostic environment preprocessing where a studying system produces artifacts for a frozen solver under a fixed budget prior to test time.
Evaluates unaided and archive-equipped meta-agents against fixed synthetic-practice and corpus-processing baselines across six heterogeneous benchmarks.
Meta-agents achieved the highest Avg@3 reward on five of six benchmarks, though fixed corpus processing performed best on the largest corpus benchmark.
Increasing study budgets did not consistently increase downstream rewards, but generated artifacts effectively shifted compute from test-time sampling to the pre-task study phase.
summary.why_it_matters: Pre-task environment study allows LLM agents to reduce compute and test-time sampling attempts needed to solve tasks in novel, unsupervised environments.

papers.title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Expert-Space Exploration Reinforcement Learning (ESRL) improves MoE post-training by perturbing router paths to enhance rollout diversity while maintaining quality through expert anchoring, entropy-adapted perturbation, and path replay.
key_points: ESRL preserves high-confidence expert anchors while restricting stochastic routing perturbations to a plausible candidate pool to prevent quality degradation.
Perturbation strength dynamically adapts based on router entropy to avoid over-perturbing routing decisions.
ESRL logs and replays the exact expert paths used during the rollout phase during policy optimization to eliminate routing mismatch.

Evaluations on Qwen3-30B-A3B show average improvements over GRPO of 3.2 percentage points on Pass@1 and 4.5 percentage points on Pass@8 across math, science, and coding tasks without extra computational cost.
summary.why_it_matters: It leverages MoE routing structures to boost rollout diversity and RL performance across multiple domains without incurring additional sampling overhead.

papers.title: MInTRL: Off-policy Intervention can boost On-policy RL

summary.tldr: MInTRL enhances on-policy reinforcement learning by using a judge policy to apply sparse, local suffix corrections during generation, expanding exploration without heavy distribution shift.
key_points: A judge-intervention policy periodically reviews rollouts, replaces incorrect suffixes with short corrections, and returns control to the base policy.
Uses a sequence-level advantage-regression training objective that eliminates the need for importance sampling.
Preserves the overall on-policy nature of trajectories while increasing exploration coverage beyond finite-budget sampling.
Demonstrates superior performance over standard on-policy and off-policy baselines across math and code benchmarks.
Ablations show effectiveness with self-intervention and across different judges, with performance peaking at moderate intervention intensity.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows models to learn from external knowledge and recover from errors during exploration without incurring the severe distribution shifts typical of fully off-policy methods.

papers.title: Ambient @ EgoProactive 2026 : Proactive Egocentric Assistance with Visually Grounded Supervision

summary.tldr: Ambient's EgoProactive submission achieved top rankings by casting proactive intervention prediction as a binary classification task and generating synthetic training data using a visually grounded, tool-calling video agent.
key_points: Replaced free-form text generation with a binary yes/no probability classification on the next token, improving macro-F1 by 0.249 and G-mean by 0.30.
Generated additional intervention timestamps using a tool-calling video agent that inspects individual video clips.
Demonstrated that visually grounded synthetic annotations outperform a narration-only synthetic dataset that was four times larger and ten times cheaper.
Ranked first in the large-model division and second overall in the EgoProactive track of the ECCV 2026 Wearable AI Challenge.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings prove that constrained binary probability outputs and visual grounding in synthetic data generation are far more effective for proactive ego-centric AI assistants than large volumes of ungrounded text.

summary.tldr: Trail of Bits reanalyzed 1Password's FLAWED report, finding its 26% AI patch success rate misleading due to flawed prompts, restricted testing, and inconsistent grading criteria.
key_points: 1Password's 26% metric included trials where prompts instructed agents to apply wrong fixes (22% of data) and modes that prohibited code compilation or testing (36% of data).
Filtering out bad-advice prompts and code-execution bans showed that 2,634 of 3,067 model-generated patches (86%) successfully blocked the supplied exploit.
Automated grading model disagreement occurred in 36.8% of cases, and self-grading models matched human reviewers on full five-category outcomes only 65.9% of the time.
Evaluation design flawed results by penalizing required test updates as regressions in 8% of ActiveMQ cases and missing an off-by-one error in 90% of Linux reference patches.
Trail of Bits released two agent skills: 'post-patch-validation' for automated testing and 'review-walkthrough' to assist human engineer code reviews.
summary.why_it_matters: Underestimating AI patching capabilities based on flawed benchmarks may unnecessarily prevent security teams from using automated tools to remediate real-world vulnerabilities.

summary.tldr: Anthropic revealed a Yemen-based threat cell used Claude models to write guidance, navigation, and control software for guided rockets, ballistic missiles, and hypersonic vehicles.
key_points: Threat actors leveraged Claude Code to write control and position estimation software, tune settings, manage firmware build pipelines, and run flight simulations for a phone-class flight computer.
The cell coordinated multiple Claude instances in delegated roles, including code generation, research, and code review.
Actors bypassed Anthropic's safeguards by obfuscating end-use goals and splitting tasks across multiple sessions to obscure intent.
The actors test-fired a guided rocket and subsequently used Claude to troubleshoot the failed flight test.
summary.why_it_matters: Generative AI systems democratize advanced software engineering expertise, enabling threat actors to accelerate the development of complex guided weapon systems.

infra.title: Accelerating Dropless MoE Training in JAX with NVIDIA Transformer Engine

summary.tldr: NVIDIA Transformer Engine accelerates dropless Mixture of Experts (MoE) training in JAX by utilizing conditional computation over shared feed-forward networks.
key_points: MoE architectures like DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mixtral achieve performance comparable to dense models using a fraction of the training compute.
Conditional computation replaces a single shared dense feed-forward network (FFN) to increase model capacity efficiently.
NVIDIA Transformer Engine provides JAX support to optimize dropless MoE training workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating Transformer Engine optimizations into JAX enables more compute-efficient training of large-scale dropless MoE models on NVIDIA GPUs.

infra.title: Announcing Pause/Resume and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU support in Dataflow

summary.tldr: Google Cloud has updated Dataflow to support Pause/Resume functionality and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.
key_points: Added support for pausing and resuming Dataflow pipelines.
Integrated NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs into Dataflow for large-scale AI workloads.
summary.why_it_matters: Users can better optimize resource usage and compute costs while running GPU-accelerated streaming and batch data processing pipelines.

infra.title: Abnormal AI: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agentic email security at scale

summary.tldr: Abnormal AI has integrated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter into its production runtime to execute agent-driven code and process data at a scale of billions of email messages.
key_points: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter provides a fully managed, serverless sandbox runtime running on ephemeral MicroVM sessions with TTLs ranging from 15 minutes to 8 hours.

The runtime supports preloaded Python and Node.js environments, handles direct API file payloads up to 100 MB or connects to Amazon S3 for larger datasets, and integrates with CloudWatch and CloudTrail.
Abnormal AI currently uses background agents to build 40 percent of its code changes end-to-end and uses agents in 80 percent of its total code changes.
Abnormal AI's email threat detection system uses a three-tiered architecture (heuristics, ML models, and agents) to process billions of messages daily and block inline threats.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how high-throughput security services can offload deterministic math, data analysis, and code verification from LLMs to secure, serverless code-execution sandboxes in production.

vendors.title: How Fyxer built an AI executive assistant people trust

summary.tldr: Fyxer has built an AI executive assistant that uses OpenAI models, fine-tuning, and memory to organize inboxes and draft emails matching individual user voices.
key_points: Leverages OpenAI models combined with fine-tuning and memory mechanisms.
Utilizes real user feedback to iteratively refine performance.
Organizes user inboxes and drafts emails personalized to each user's specific voice.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining fine-tuning and memory with user feedback allows AI assistants to reliably mirror personalized communication styles for inbox management.
